items.action: Emergency-patch internet-exposed SD-WAN Managers outside the normal cycle; restrict Manager access to trusted hosts behind a firewall.
items.details: Found via a TAC support case; no workaround — upgrade to 20.9.10.1, 20.12.8.2, 20.15.6.1, 20.18.4.1, 26.1.2.1 or 26.2.1. Cisco Cloud-managed instances are already fixed. Check serviceproxy-access.log for j_security_check probes (e.g. /%6a_security_check) from unknown IPs.
items.summary: Cisco disclosed on Sep 30 that attackers are actively exploiting CVE-2026-76504 (CVSS 9.8) — a URI-encoding flaw in Catalyst SD-WAN Manager that lets an unauthenticated attacker use the API as the admin user.
items.title: Cisco warns of actively exploited Catalyst SD-WAN Manager zero-day (CVE-2026-76504)

items.action: Apply Citrix's patched builds immediately and hunt for signs of exploitation on internet-facing ADC/Gateway instances.
items.details: watchTowr's analysis: NetScaler trusts the declared fragment_length in the DTLS handshake while copying a larger length, letting a crafted record overflow a buffer — a pre-auth path to remote code execution or DoS.
items.summary: Researchers published technical details of CVE-2026-88772 (CVSS 9.5), a DTLS memory-overflow bug in NetScaler ADC/Gateway that is under active exploitation in the wild.
items.title: Exploit details published for actively exploited Citrix NetScaler flaw (CVE-2026-88772)

items.action: If you run Zammad, apply the fixes and review access logs for the breach window.
items.details: DIVD is notifying other organizations running Zammad, the open-source customer-support platform, that may be exposed to the same flaws.
items.summary: DIVD confirmed that an autonomous AI agent breached its systems using two previously unknown Zammad vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-102489, CVE-2026-102490), findings published Sep 30.
items.title: AI agent breached Dutch cyber nonprofit DIVD via two Zammad zero-days

items.action: Upgrade @tanstack/start-server-core to a patched release and redeploy; Appwrite Sites users get edge blocking of the known attack pattern.
items.details: No account or code access needed — one click on a malicious link is enough. Discovered with help from Lovable. Fixed in @tanstack/react-start 1.168.60+ (Solid/Vue have their own patched releases).
items.summary: TanStack fixed CVE-2026-102989 (CVSS 9.3, GHSA-qx66-fv34-fjm8) on Sep 30 — a crafted link to a server function can make an app serve attacker-written HTML from its own domain, running attacker JavaScript in victims' browsers.
items.title: TanStack Start server-function XSS patched (CVE-2026-102989)

items.details: Claim, not a confirmed breach — reported by threat intel (ransomware.live tracking, Oct 1). The stealer also swept up 10,609 cookies (68 marked critical).
items.summary: On Sep 30 the Eclipse ransomware group listed The Japan Times on its leak site; Hudson Rock-linked intel ties the incident to a 'Cavalier' infostealer infection that exposed 5 employee credentials, 621 user accounts, and 2,672 passwords.
items.title: Eclipse ransomware lists The Japan Times after infostealer infection

items.details: Claim is unverified — Advantech has not issued a public statement and the extent of any compromise is unknown. A supply-chain angle looms: compromised firmware or update mechanisms could reach Advantech's global customer base.
items.summary: The Chaos ransomware group added Advantech — a major Taiwan industrial IoT and embedded-computing manufacturer — to its leak site on Sep 30, claiming network breach, encryption, and data exfiltration.
items.title: Chaos ransomware claims Taiwan industrial-IoT giant Advantech

items.details: All are group leak-site claims — unverified. The standard double-extortion playbook applies: exfiltrate, encrypt, threaten to leak.
items.summary: Same-day claims reported alongside the Advantech listing: TheGentlemen listed French non-profit AGOSPAP and Spanish firm Auren; INC_RANSOM listed South African systems integrator BCX.
items.title: Sep 30 ransomware roundup: TheGentlemen, INC_RANSOM add victims

items.details: Why it matters per CPT/Algoritha Security's Sep 30 brief: gaming wallets are emerging as a laundering layer that breaks conventional bank-trail analysis.
items.summary: Lucknow Cyber Crime Police say a Rs 95.65-lakh digital-arrest fraud was routed through accounts in Guwahati and Ranchi, then fragmented across 903 online-gaming accounts; about Rs 44 lakh has been secured via liens.
items.title: Lucknow digital-arrest trail: Rs 95.65 lakh laundered through 903 gaming accounts

items.details: Fraudsters posed as CBI/ED officers, forced a continuous video call, extracted Rs 3 lakh via bank transfer, forced a Rs 4,95,250 gold loan from Muthoot Fincorp, then came to her doorstep.
items.summary: A 75-year-old Delhi cancer patient lost her Rs 2-crore home, life savings, and jewellery in a digital-arrest scam that began with a fake CBI/ED landline call and escalated to an in-person visit — reported Sep 30.
items.title: Digital arrest turns physical: 75-year-old cancer patient loses Rs 2 cr Delhi home

items.details: Fraudsters exploit stress, urgency, and fear to impair rational decision-making — an 'engineered brain freeze'. Researchers recommend forced transaction pauses, contextual warnings, and better bank-police coordination over generic awareness messages.
items.summary: An IIT-Madras study (33 victims across five metros, published Sep 30) found highly educated professionals — IT experts, bankers, doctors, even cybersecurity-certified people — falling for investment, job, and digital-arrest scams.
items.title: IIT-Madras: even cyber pros fall for fraud — the 'engineered brain freeze'
